newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish stocks seen in sideways drift next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish stocks seen in sideways drift next week.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse is likely to extend its sideways drift, with no fresh signals in sight to spur an uptrend or a fall, analysts said.

"The market has stopped on a certain level about three weeks ago ... and it still seems to be waiting for an impulse, but...I see no signals which could give it a direction next week," said Dariusz Szepieniec of Bank Slaski brokerage.

Analysts said neither the statistical office's business climate survey results for November, due on Thursday nor the food prices figures for the last 10 days of November, seen on Friday, were likely to be such signals.

They said the central bank deputy head's comments earlier this week on a possible rise in interest rates could make some investors feel less confident but that few considered a rise in official rates a real threat unless inflation surges.

Some analysts said, however, this week's official GDP data showing 7.3 percent year-on-year growth in the third quarter, offered some grounds for optimism making the government's 5.5 percent growth target for 1996 easily achievable.
"The forecasts that GDP should grow this year by 5.5 percent or more are a good sign -- at mid-year such a prediction was considered optimistic," said Rafal Lis, an analyst at BGZ brokerage.
Next week is likely to see less action on the primary market amid a year-end flood of new issues with a small offering in Elpo jeans maker ending on Thursday.
The WIG index rose 0.9 percent this week to close at 13,789.7 points on Friday.

Espebepe was this week's top gainer, rising 12.9 percent and analysts said the growth was a reaction to its 50-percent plunge since October 22, when the company's new management announced it might go bankrupt unless it reached a far reaching debt-reduction deal with its creditors.
Other top gainers were Animex, which rose 10.2 percent and Farm Food, which gained 8.4 percent.
The biggest losers were Remak, which fell 6.8 percent and Mostostal Gdansk, which fell 5.4 percent.
Six new stocks will be added on Monday to the 15 issues already traded in the continuous trade system.
Agros will trade in blocks of 100 shares, Kety of 25, Mostostal Export of 1,000, Polifarb Cieszyn of 500, Wedel and Zywiec of 50.
